title: Celesta Health - Procurement / MSA & DPA Review
summary: Redwood AE/SE reviewed the standard MSA and DPA with Celesta Health procurement/legal/security. Discussed SLA commitments for Dedicated vs Hosted, encryption/KMS, SSO/SAML, and pricing thresholds for committed capacity. Customer requested redlines around indemnity and data handling, and wants security pack and SOC2 docs. Agreed to send redlined MSA, pricing worksheet, and schedule vendor onboarding call with infra team next week.
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack + SOC2 cert link (Maya) by 2027-01-12
Redwood to share redlined MSA and DPA template (Diego) by 2027-01-14
Schedule vendor onboarding with Celesta infra (Tom + Diego) week of 2027-01-18
Customer to provide preferred PO terms and legal contact details (Rachel) by 2027-01-13
action_items: Maya - email SOC2 + security pack link - due 2027-01-12
Diego - prepare redline draft of MSA/DPA and technical appendix - due 2027-01-14
Rachel - confirm PO payment terms and share legal contact - due 2027-01-13
Tom - provide network/VPC diagram and expected throughput for pilot - due 2027-01-15
transcript:
Header: 2027-01-10 16:00 PST | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Olivia (Redwood SE), Rachel (Celesta Procurement), Dr. Alan Pierce (CTO), Sanjay (Security), Leah (Legal), Tom (DevOps)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you carving time out, we'll run through the MSA and DPA items and then Diego will jump into any technical SLAs.
[00:18] Rachel: Thanks Maya, quick note, we've got Leah from legal and Sanjay from security on the line, we mostly want to understand the non-negotiables and what we need to pull together for procurement.
[00:30] Diego: Great, I'll be as concrete as possible. First high level — Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) options. For enterprise deployments like what you described we usually recommend Dedicated or Private depending on network isolation needs.
[00:47] Dr. Alan: For us, latency at peak matters more than absolute lowest cost — we're doing real-time triage workflows so sub-200ms P95 is desirable. Can you give an SLA statement that maps to that?
[00:58] Diego: Right — our Dedicated offering has a 99.9% uptime SLA and latency targets that we can baseline in the SLO appendix. We can commit to regional latency targets and provide tracing for sample endpoints. Important to note, the SLA ties to node availability and capacity - there are conditions around sequencing for rolling upgrades.
[01:18] Leah: On the MSA side, we had several redlines around indemnity and data retention. We need clarity on what Redwood deletes vs retains for hosted logs and whether you support customer-managed KMS for keys.
[01:30] Maya: Totally, so for Hosted we retain request logs for 30 days by default, and DPA options allow different retention policies. We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and Dedicated can integrate with your KMS via our IAM/KMS connectors. I'll send the security pack that outlines KMS/HSM options.
[01:49] Sanjay: When you say integrate with KMS, do you mean keys are never in Redwood plaintext, or are there any pass-through components? We need crypto details for our audit.
[02:00] Diego: Keys are customer-managed in the Private case, meaning our control plane doesn't hold key material; in Dedicated we can do a KMS proxy config. I will include a technical appendix that covers key lifecycle, envelope encryption, and where logs are stored (and redaction options).
[02:16] Rachel: On pricing and procurement, procurement needs a committed capacity quote and annual cost for budgeting. What's the minimum commit and how flexible is the billing?
[02:27] Maya: Our typical entry for Dedicated is a 6-12 month commit; we can do quarterly billing but PO terms are usually net30 or net45 depending on procurement. For pilot we can offer a short-term test at discounted rates—we've put free credits for onboarding in the playbook. For large commits we provide unit pricing for tokens and a reserved throughput SLA.
[02:47] Tom: For onboarding, we'll need an IP allowlist and an expected throughput number so we can confirm VPC peering and routing. Also need info on VPN or direct connect options.
[02:57] Diego: Yes — we support VPC peering, AWS Transit Gateway, and on-prem direct connect. I'll send a network diagram and the peering checklist. Also note that prefix/KV cache behavior can affect throughput — if you have long context sessions we recommend Dedicated with KV-optimized configs.
[03:17] Leah: A couple legal asks — can you confirm the DPA references GDPR articles and provides subprocessors list? And do you support data residency in EU regions?
[03:28] Maya: The DPA template includes GDPR references and you can request an EU-only deployment for data residency; we have regions in EU-West. We'll attach the subprocessors list in the security pack.
[03:39] Rachel: Timeline wise, we want to finalize pricing and MSA approvals before 2027-01-31 so finance can sign a PO. Any blockers?
[03:47] Maya: We can aim for that. Typical blockers are long legal redlines and SOC2 review timelines — that's why I'll send SOC2 + penetration testing docs right after this call.
[03:58] Sanjay: One item — we require audit logs retention for 1 year and an API to retrieve logs for audits. Do you expose a logs API or is that part of the enterprise package?
[04:11] Diego: We offer log export to your S3 bucket for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we can arrange an export schedule or longer retention as an add-on. The audit logs API is available on enterprise plans.
[04:24] Dr. Alan: Can you speak to model version pinning and rollback? We need deterministic outputs for clinical inference; if a model update changes behavior, we need ability to pin a version and revert quickly.
[04:37] Diego: Yes — model pinning is supported; the runtime supports model variants and automatic fallback. We'll include the rollout/rollback policy language in the technical appendix — you can pin at the route level.
[04:49] Maya: Quick note — procurement sometimes asks about indemnity caps and liability. Our standard MSA has limited liability with carveouts for gross negligence; we see a range of customer requests here but we'll accept redlines within reason.
[05:02] Leah: We'll prepare initial redlines and upload to the shared drive. Who should they send to?
[05:08] Maya: Please send to maya@redwood.com and cc legal@redwood.com — Diego will be on copy for the technical bits.
[05:15] Rachel: On pricing, can you send a worksheet with committed tiers and expected token throughput so finance can run numbers? Also we need an estimate for overage charges.
[05:26] Maya: Absolutely — I'm going to attach a pricing worksheet; committed tiers include baseline throughput, reserved vCPU/GPU units, and token rates. Overages are billed at a defined per-token rate, and there's a graduated discount for larger contracts.
[05:39] Tom: For the pilot, we want to run a week-long latency/cost benchmark — what's the best path? Do we provision a small Dedicated pool or run against Hosted with a workload capture?
[05:50] Diego: For representative latency testing, Dedicated is better since it isolates jitter; however, you can start with Hosted using a warm-up pattern to measure baseline. For KV cache and long-context tests, Dedicated gives closer performance to production. We can spin up a small Dedicated pilot environment for a week as part of a POC; that'll require a short-term commit.
[06:10] Rachel: What's the typical approval flow inside Redwood for DPA redlines? We want to understand time to negotiate.
[06:18] Maya: Minor redlines can be routed through our legal ops in 3-5 business days; complex indemnity or data residency negotiations may take 2-3 weeks. We'll flag anything that looks like a dealbreaker early.
[06:29] Leah: We also need SAML/SSO details and SCIM for provisioning. Can you confirm SSO options?
[06:37] Diego: We support SAML, OIDC, and SCIM provisioning for user management. I'll include the SSO integration guide. Apologies if earlier transcription call said 'Samuel' — that's SAML.
[06:49] Maya: A few practical next steps — I'll send SOC2 and security pack by Thursday, Diego will prepare the redline-friendly MSA and tech appendix, and we'll share the pricing worksheet so you can prep a PO.
[07:03] Rachel: Great. On payment terms — finance prefers net45 but can do net30 if we get an early payment discount. Would Redwood consider a 2% 15-day discount?
[07:15] Maya: I can flag that for commercial; discounts for early payment are possible on enterprise contracts. I'll propose that to my manager and get back to you.
[07:25] Sanjay: One more security question — do you provide pentest results or summary? We need evidence for our supply chain audit.
[07:32] Diego: We have a redacted pentest summary and a vulnerability management policy we can share under an NDA. It's included in the security pack.
[07:41] Tom: Regarding network setup: will there be a static egress IP or a range? We need to set firewall rules.
[07:48] Diego: For VPC peering there's no egress NAT; for Hosted you'll have a published egress IP range per region. I'll include the exact CIDR ranges and the allowlist steps.
[07:58] Leah: For the DPA, define subprocessor notification cadence — we prefer 30-day notice before onboarding a new subprocessor. Is that acceptable?
[08:07] Maya: 30 days is workable in many cases; we'll check the subprocessors policy and confirm.
[08:14] Rachel: Okay, that covers main items. Anything else from the Redwood side?
[08:19] Olivia: Just to add, we'll also include a short runbook for onboarding with steps: IP allowlist, SSO setup, initial benchmarks, and model pinning checklist.
[08:29] Dr. Alan: Good. After we review the redlines, what's the SLA for finalizing? We want to avoid back-and-forth for more than two weeks.
[08:36] Maya: We'll prioritize you for a two-week turnaround if redlines are reasonably scoped; complex changes may take longer. We'll aim to close before your month-end target.
[08:45] Rachel: Excellent. Let's recap the action items and owners.
[08:49] Maya: Recap — Maya sends SOC2/security pack and pricing worksheet; Diego sends redline MSA/DPA and tech appendix; Tom to share network diagram and throughput numbers; Rachel to confirm PO terms and legal contact.
[08:59] Leah: We'll upload initial redlines by Friday and share comments in the doc.
[09:04] Maya: Perfect, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the onboarding session.
[09:12] (end)
